A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same COMPACT study despite the changed title. Their main text, tables, figures, mathematical notation, and Appendices A–C are sufficiently readable and complete for reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original model-training and benchmark results, including Table 2, ablations, dataset analyses, and the open-source-generator experiment in Appendix A.7.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark results, ablations, dataset analyses, and the Appendix A.7 generator experiment. Results retained from v2 still qualify as original empirical results.

M1.justification: The ten-capability taxonomy and four-step sampling, generation, verification, and dataset-assembly procedure are retained. Section 3.2 newly specifies uniform sampling, but does not establish a change from the earlier implementation. The reorganized appendix prompts retain their contents.

E1.justification: Both versions use LLaVA-665K training data, the same eight benchmarks in Section 4.1, and the additional OK-VQA, MMMU, and MMMU-Pro evaluations. No datasets, domains, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the full-data and random baselines, EL2N, Perplexity, SemDeDup, D2-Pruning, Self-Sup, Self-Filter, and ICONS. The Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct generator comparison also already appears in v2 Table 9, corresponding to v3 Table 10.

E3.justification: The LLaVA-v1.5-7B-LoRA model, one-epoch training, 32K compositional samples plus approximately 33K VIT samples, and 16K compositional-data analysis settings are retained. Inspection finds no substantive revisions to splits, metrics, budgets, or experimental controls.

E4.justification: Complexity matching, complexity-range and VIT-mixture ablations, capability-removal experiments, token and failure-mode analyses, generator comparisons, and qualitative cases are retained. Their renumbering and relocation introduce no new analytical questions or evidence.

E5.justification: Figure 3 now identifies the existing shaded bands as ±1 standard deviation across three runs; v2 did not explain them. Figure 1 additionally documents kernel density estimation with bandwidth 5. These clarify statistical reporting without establishing that additional runs were performed.

E6.justification: Section 4.3 changes the reported proportion of zero-capability questions from 0.9% to 1.1%, matching the 1.1% already reported in Appendix C.2. Benchmark scores, plotted curves and bands, ablation results, and qualitative findings otherwise remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Complexity remains the number of required atomic capabilities, with the same relationship between sampled and resulting complexity. Shortened taxonomy descriptions and notation corrections do not change the mathematics. Neither version adds different assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that composing atomic capabilities improves data efficiency, achieving 100.2% relative performance with approximately 10% of the original data and gains on MM-Vet and MMStar. The new title and visual-compositional-tuning terminology retain the contributions' scientific scope.

C2.justification: The information-density explanation, need for both simple and complex samples, capability-overlap discussion, and generator-bias and knowledge-task limitations are retained. The expanded verification rationale restates capability-mismatch failures already discussed in v2 Appendix A.6.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies uniform capability sampling and Figure 1's density-estimation bandwidth. Section 5 removes v2's explicit promise to publicly release generated data, while retaining the project link. Generation hyperparameters, prompts, time, and cost are unchanged; actual data-access loss is not established.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to instruction tuning, compositional reasoning, and data selection are retained. The changed Liu et al. citation suffix refers to the same work already listed in both bibliographies.

P1.justification: v3 adopts the title Visual Compositional Tuning and a conference header, standardizes terminology, copyedits prose, and shortens taxonomy descriptions. Appendix B's prompts are reordered, but the main narrative and section hierarchy remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The appendices undergo substantial display reorganization: v2 Figure 9 becomes the enlarged Table 4, the capability-ablation table uses paired columns, and qualitative figures move beside their explanations. Generation prompts are split and regrouped, eliminating footer overlap. Table 1 and Figure 3 are also restyled, including larger plot labels and revised tick placement.

improvement.justification: v3 improves readability and reporting by explaining Figure 3's uncertainty bands and run count, reconciling the zero-capability statistic, and repairing the appendix layout. The method and substantive experimental evidence remain stable, limiting the overall gain. Removing the explicit data-release promise weakens the documented sharing commitment, although the PDFs do not establish any actual loss of access.
